children: Australian shares ended flat on Wednesday as gains in mining stocks on firmer commodity prices countered losses in banks, while investors awaited monthly jobs data for cues on the central bank's monetary policy outlook beyond September.
rose 0.1% to 8,765.30 points. It ended 0.3% higher on Tuesday.
Markets awaited the August employment data due on Thursday for hints on the Reserve Bank of Australia's monetary tightening outlook following the widely expected hawkish move next week.
RBA Governor Michele Bullock said on Tuesday that unemployment in a range of 4.5% to 5.0% could help control inflation, hinting some rise might be needed from the current level of 4.5%.

"Beyond September, core inflation and employment figures will continue to shape the future direction of rates, while elevated geopolitical tensions and high oil prices suggest that the higher-for-longer interest rate environment is more likely to persist,” said Cliff Man, CEO of ETF Shares.

Financials are being dragged by continued weakness in the property market, while intense competition for home loans continues to put downward pressure on banks' net interest margins, Man said.
